test_outcomes: I opened the app on the chat screen with the ghost top-right. I pressed the ghost. The screen changed to 'Incognito chat' and the ghost was replaced by an X in the same corner. The keyboard also opened by itself, which I had not asked for. I pressed the X. The 'Incognito chat' title went away, the normal greeting came back, and the ghost was back in the corner. The incognito X was still visible top-right, dimmed behind it, so there were two identical X marks on one screen. I pressed the panel's X. Only the panel closed and I stayed in the incognito chat. So the two X marks did two different jobs, close this panel versus leave incognito, and each did what I had predicted. Nothing written on screen said which was which. I relied on position, the top-left X sitting on the panel and the top-right one under the 'Incognito chat' title, and it held. I finished it.

tester.evidence: tester-built group (grouping correction): the "Claude" wordmark at the top of the drawer (gg13), whose function the detector could not settle, starts a new chat exactly as "+ New chat" does — all 7 tapped live, each opened a fresh empty composer with the keyboard up. Both renderings co-occur on every drawer screen (screen2, screen18, screen33), same surface, same scope. Confusion bullets that apply: (1) a user who learned "+ New chat" has no way to recognise the wordmark as the same job — it is drawn as a title, not a button; (2) the two co-occur on one screen with nothing tying them together. No justification bullet holds: it is not a different surface or scope, and the wordmark is less explicit, not more, and does not look like what it is (a control). Nothing sighted says the title is pressable, so a user who taps it to read or to go "home" is dropped into a new chat.

findings.recommendation: make the drawer wordmark a plain, non-interactive title and leave "+ New chat" as the single rendering of the job; if the title must stay pressable, give it the same "+ New chat" treatment so it reads as that action

findings.disagreement_note: the tester found the ghost and the X are the two faces of one toggle in one fixed corner, with "Incognito chat" written when the X shows; Gopal, Kwame and Yuki each said they could not connect the X to the ghost, and each held that view, softened, after testing

tester.evidence: all 10 tapped live: every ghost switched the chat to incognito and every X switched it back, in place. The two appearances are the two faces of one toggle in one fixed position (top-right of the composer screen): the ghost is shown while incognito is off, the X while it is on. Justification: the alternate rendering is more explicit, not less — the X is the conventional "leave this" mark, and when it shows, "Incognito chat" is written directly under the top bar and the ghost is drawn large in the middle, so a user who pressed the ghost meets the X together with the words naming what the X leaves.
